definitions.ask: Should `-F` also overwrite your edits to rows still in the note?
definitions.why: You asked -F to disregard edits; status, children, and sessions stay safe either way

choices.label: Present rows get Google's time, title, badges, and root back; status, children, history stay
Present rows stay exactly as they are; `-F` only restores missing rows and links

definitions.ask: When all of today's Bob rows and the Events stamp vanish at once, should sync hold, not tombstone?
definitions.why: Never re-adds without consent, yet never mistakes a clobbered note for your deletions

choices.label: Sync writes nothing that day and says the note was replaced; `bob gcal sync -F` restores it
Sync re-adds the lost rows on its next run; a deliberately wiped section comes back once
Keep today's rule; each missing row counts as your deletion and only `-F` restores it

definitions.ask: Should force use bob's usual `-F|--force` rather than `-f`, which sync already uses for `--format`?
definitions.why: bob spells force `-F` wherever `-f` is `--format` (plugins sync, periods, freshness)

choices.label: `-F|--force`; `-f` stays `--format` as on every gcal command and in the create hook
`-f|--force` as asked; sync's `--format` moves to `-F`, a `!` break for `-f json` callers

definitions.ask: Add the decision record `decisions:gcal-force-resets-the-day` for the reset and replaced-section rule?
definitions.requested: As a part of this change, let's add a new `-f|--force` option to the `bob gcal sync` command that disregards any previous edits/deletions and re-writes the appropriate event tasks and pomodoros to today's daily file as if it were the first time that command were run for that day.

definitions.ask: Mark `decisions:bob-gcal-is-read-only-and-proposes-once` partly superseded by the new record?
definitions.corrects: deleted rows are tombstoned and never re-added

strands: Bob Gcal Is Read Only And Proposes Once
